- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat or negative; apply a 0.8–1.2% upward bias if sentiment <0.3 for 3+ days.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply 10–15% smoothing or lag correction if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.0 → 0.8), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
